title: Vegan and Vegetarian Michelin Star Restaurants ({{guideYear}} List)
description: Every Michelin-starred restaurant that serves no meat or fish, the starred restaurants with vegetarian tasting menus, and London’s. Checked October 2026.
h1: Vegan and Vegetarian Michelin Star Restaurants
summary: The starred restaurants that serve no meat at all, where to find a vegetarian tasting menu, and London’s best options.
figure: {{vegFree}} meat-free starred restaurants; {{vegMenu}} vegetarian tasting menus
body:
{{vegFree}} Michelin-starred restaurants serve no meat or fish, {{vegFreeVegan}} of them fully vegan or plant-based, from Arpège in Paris, the only one with three stars, to Plates London. Far more will cook for you: {{vegMenu}} starred restaurants offer a vegetarian tasting menu, and {{vegan}} list vegan options.

That makes vegetarian and vegan Michelin star restaurants easier to find than their small number suggests. Below is every meat-free restaurant with a Michelin star, with its price, then the cities and three-star restaurants with the most vegetarian menus, a full list for London, and what the MICHELIN Guide’s diet labels promise. Every figure comes from the current guide editions, checked {{checked}}.

Every vegan and vegetarian Michelin star restaurant

The {{vegFree}} meat-free restaurants with a star are spread over {{vegFreeCountries}} countries: {{vegFreeSplit}}. Switzerland, China and the United States have four each. In Switzerland they are OZ, ZOE, Neue Taverne and KLE; in China, King’s Joy and Lamdre in Beijing and Fu He Hui in Shanghai hold two stars each and draw on the country’s Buddhist vegetarian cooking. Italy and Germany have three, among them Joia in Milan and Davide Guidara’s two-star I Tenerumi on the island of Vulcano.

About a third are fully vegan. Seven Swans in Frankfurt, Bonvivant in Berlin, KLE in Zurich, JOLA in Vienna, Légume in Seoul, Fabrik in Austin and Plates London cook without any animal products at all, and so do the plant-based De Nieuwe Winkel in Nijmegen, Fields by René Mathieu in Luxembourg and MITA in Washington, DC. The vegetarian ones may use dairy and eggs, though most will make their menu vegan with notice.

{{table:veg-free}}

Is there a three-Michelin-star vegan restaurant?

Yes, almost. Alain Passard’s Arpège in Paris, which has held three stars since 1996, has cooked only plants since 21 July 2025: vegetables, fruit, herbs and flowers, many from its own gardens, with honey from its hives the one animal product left. Its dinner menu, Cuisine de la Terre, costs {{dinner:arpege}} and lunch {{lunch:arpege}}, both with service included, according to the restaurant’s own menus.

Eleven Madison Park in New York held three stars as a fully vegan restaurant from its reopening in 2021 until October 2025, when Daniel Humm put a few meat and seafood dishes back on the menu. The tasting menu is still mostly plant-based, and a fully vegan version is still offered, at {{dinner:eleven-madison-park}}. No other vegetarian restaurant has three stars today: the two-star King’s Joy, Fu He Hui, Lamdre, I Tenerumi and De Nieuwe Winkel come closest.

The first vegetarian and vegan restaurants to win a star

Joia in Milan was the first vegetarian restaurant in Europe to win a Michelin star, in 1996, and still holds it, now under Sauro Ricci and Raffaele Minghini after founder Pietro Leemann stepped back in 2024. The first fully vegan star is disputed. Seven Swans in Frankfurt already held a star as a vegetarian restaurant when chef Ricky Saward made its menu fully vegan at the end of 2019, and has kept it since. In January 2021 Claire Vallée’s ONA, near Bordeaux, became the first vegan restaurant in France to win one; it closed in 2022.

Several have followed. Plates London, Kirk Haworth’s 25-seat dining room in Shoreditch, became the first vegan restaurant in Britain with a star in February 2025, and Légume in Seoul the first in Asia, according to the MICHELIN Guide. Bonvivant in Berlin went fully vegan in early 2026, and the newest, Fabrik in Austin, won its star in the Texas guide revealed on 8 October 2026.

Michelin star vegetarian restaurants in London

Among Michelin star vegan restaurants, London has just one: Plates London in Shoreditch, whose ten-course discovery menu costs {{dinner:plates-london}}. It is the place to go if you want a meal with no animal products and no adjustments. For everything else, {{vegMenu_london}} of London’s {{londonTotal}} starred restaurants offer a vegetarian tasting menu and {{vegan_london}} list vegan options, so {{vegAny_london}} in all can feed you well.

Four of London’s three-star restaurants have a vegetarian tasting menu: Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester, which also lists vegan options, Hélène Darroze at The Connaught, Restaurant Gordon Ramsay and Sketch’s Lecture Room and Library. CORE by Clare Smyth lists vegan options. For less, London’s Indian restaurants are hard to beat for vegetarians: Amaya’s tasting menu costs {{dinner:amaya}} and its set lunch {{lunch:amaya}}, and Trishna, Gymkhana, Benares, Quilon and Jamavar all have vegetarian tasting menus. Our London Michelin star restaurants page has every one’s prices.

{{table:veg-london}}

Where to find the most vegetarian tasting menus

London has the most starred restaurants with a vegetarian menu, ahead of Paris and Hong Kong. Berlin is the easiest city of all for vegetarians, though: 14 of its 19 starred restaurants offer one, and two serve no meat at all. Munich, Zurich and Frankfurt offer one at about half their starred restaurants, while Tokyo, with more starred restaurants than any other city, has only a handful.

{{table:veg-cities}}

Three-star restaurants with a vegetarian tasting menu

{{vegMenu3}} of the world’s {{n3}} three-star restaurants list a vegetarian menu, about {{vegMenuPct3}}, and {{vegan3}} list vegan options. France has the most, from Mirazur in Menton to Anne-Sophie Pic’s restaurant in Valence. Our list of every three-Michelin-star restaurant has the rest.

{{table:veg-3}}

What the MICHELIN Guide’s vegetarian and vegan labels mean

The MICHELIN Guide lists special diets on each restaurant’s page and in its search filters, as each restaurant reports them. “Vegetarian menu” means a separate vegetarian tasting menu, which {{vegMenu}} starred restaurants offer ({{vegMenuPct}}). “Vegan options” ({{vegan}}, or {{veganPct}}) and “Vegetarian options” ({{vegOpt}}, or {{vegOptPct}}) mean the kitchen can adapt dishes, usually with notice. Fully meat-free restaurants are filed under a vegetarian or vegan cuisine instead.

Say so when you book, not when you sit down: a tasting menu is planned days ahead. If you’re vegan, ask about butter, cream, eggs, honey and fish or meat stocks, which turn up in dishes that look like vegetables. The same goes for halal options and kosher ones: the labels describe what a restaurant says it can do, not a certificate.

How much does a vegan Michelin star meal cost?

The cheapest meat-free starred tasting menus cost {{dinner:racines-bruno-cirino}}, at Racines – Bruno Cirino in Nice and at Fields by René Mathieu in Luxembourg; Mi Xun Teahouse in Chengdu is cheaper still, at a typical spend of {{dinner:mi-xun-teahouse}}. Most cost between $150 and $250 before drinks. A vegetarian menu at a restaurant that also serves meat usually costs the same as the main one or a little less, and set lunches cost less again: our guide to the cheapest Michelin star restaurants lists the lowest prices everywhere.

faq.q: Are there vegan Michelin star restaurants in Paris?
faq.a: One: Arpège, Alain Passard’s three-star restaurant, which has cooked only plants since July 2025, with honey from its own hives the one exception. Its dinner menu costs {{dinner:arpege}}. {{vegMenu_paris}} starred restaurants in Paris, Arpège included, offer a vegetarian tasting menu.

faq.q: Are there vegan Michelin star restaurants in New York?
faq.a: Dirt Candy, Amanda Cohen’s vegetarian restaurant on the Lower East Side, holds one star; its tasting menu costs {{dinner:dirt-candy}}. Eleven Madison Park, vegan from 2021 to 2025, still offers a fully vegan tasting menu, and {{vegan_new_york}} of New York’s starred restaurants list vegan options.

faq.q: Which US Michelin star restaurants are vegetarian?
faq.a: Four: Dirt Candy in New York, MITA and Oyster Oyster in Washington, DC (Oyster Oyster’s only non-vegetarian dish is an optional oyster), and Fabrik in Austin, which is vegan.
